project_title: Foundational Probability Theory for Computer Science
subject: Discrete Mathematics & Computational Stochastics
author: Prof. Locus AI Studio

slides.title: Uncertainty in Distributed Systems
slides.subtitle: When Determinism Fails at Scale

theory_fragments.content: Modern distributed architectures (DHTs, consensus engines, cloud meshes) cannot assume deterministic packet delivery or collision-free hashing.
Engineering Failure: In a network of $N = 10^6$ nodes with independent link failure probability $p = 10^{-4}$, the probability of at least one partition exceeds $99.999%$.
P(\text{Failure}) = 1 - (1 - p)^N \approx 1 - e^{-Np} \to 1.0
Rigorous probability space $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, P)$ formalizes stochastic guarantees in algorithm design.

slides.speaker_notes: Introduce the distributed hash collision and link failure problem to ground abstract probability in concrete CSE infrastructure.

slides.title: Sample Spaces & Event Algebras
slides.subtitle: The Geometry of Outcomes

theory_fragments.content: The **sample space** $\Omega$ is the set of all mutually exclusive primitive computational outcomes.
An **event algebra** $\mathcal{F} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\Omega)$ is a $\sigma$-algebra closed under complementation and countable unions:
1.\; \Omega \in \mathcal{F}, \quad 2.\; E \in \mathcal{F} \implies E^c \in \mathcal{F}, \quad 3.\; \{E_i\}_{i=1}^\infty \subseteq \mathcal{F} \implies \bigcup_{i=1}^\infty E_i \in \mathcal{F}
In discrete CSE settings, $\mathcal{F} = \mathcal{P}(\Omega)$. In continuous runtime spaces, $\mathcal{F}$ is the Borel $\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R})$.

slides.speaker_notes: Establish set-theoretic rigor. Explain why arbitrary subsets cannot always be measured in continuous spaces, motivating sigma-algebras.

slides.title: The Kolmogorov Axioms
slides.subtitle: Measure-Theoretic Foundations

theory_fragments.content: A **probability measure** is a function $P: \mathcal{F} \to [0, 1]$ satisfying Kolmogorov's three core axioms:
\text{Axiom 1 (Non-negativity): } P(E) \ge 0, \quad \forall E \in \mathcal{F}
\text{Axiom 2 (Unitarity): } P(\Omega) = 1
\text{Axiom 3 (}\sigma\text{-Additivity): } E_i \cap E_j = \emptyset \implies P\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^\infty E_i\right) = \sum_{i=1}^\infty P(E_i)

slides.speaker_notes: Demonstrate the probability simplex geometry. Stress that probability is normalized volume or measure over the space.

slides.title: Inclusion-Exclusion Principle
slides.subtitle: Analytical Derivation from Additivity

theory_fragments.content: For non-disjoint events $A, B \in \mathcal{F}$, direct addition double-counts the intersection measure:
A \cup B = A \cup (B \setminus (A \cap B)) \quad \text{where disjoint}
P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B \setminus (A \cap B))
P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B)

slides.speaker_notes: Derive union probability algebraically. Show how subtracting the overlap corrects the metric volume.

slides.title: Conditional Probability
slides.subtitle: Relativizing the Subspace Universe

theory_fragments.content: When prior knowledge dictates event $B$ occurred ($P(B) > 0$), $\Omega$ collapses to the sub-universe $B$.
P(A \mid B) \triangleq \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)}
Multiplication Rule: $P(A \cap B) = P(B) P(A \mid B) = P(A) P(B \mid A)$.
Chain Rule for $n$ sequential compute events: $P(\bigcap_{i=1}^n A_i) = \prod_{i=1}^n P(A_i \mid \bigcap_{j=1}^{i-1} A_j)$.

slides.speaker_notes: Emphasize conditional probability as renormalization: dividing by P(B) scales the remaining universe back to unit measure 1.

slides.title: Law of Total Probability
slides.subtitle: Partitioning State Spaces

theory_fragments.content: Let $\{B_1, B_2, \dots, B_k\}$ form a finite disjoint partition of $\Omega$, such that $\bigcup_{i=1}^k B_i = \Omega$ and $B_i \cap B_j = \emptyset$.
A = A \cap \Omega = A \cap \left( \bigcup_{i=1}^k B_i \right) = \bigcup_{i=1}^k (A \cap B_i)
P(A) = \sum_{i=1}^k P(A \cap B_i) = \sum_{i=1}^k P(A \mid B_i) P(B_i)
Foundation for Markov state decomposition, branch prediction, and recursive algorithmic cost analysis.

slides.speaker_notes: Walk through partitioning geometrically. Show that summing over mutually exclusive slices reconstructs event A.

slides.title: Bayes' Theorem & Inference
slides.subtitle: Inverting Causal Observations

theory_fragments.content: Bayesian inversion updates a prior hypothesis probability $P(B_j)$ upon observing algorithmic symptom $A$:
P(B_j \mid A) = \frac{P(A \cap B_j)}{P(A)}
P(B_j \mid A) = \frac{P(A \mid B_j) P(B_j)}{\sum_{i=1}^k P(A \mid B_i) P(B_i)}
Posterior $\propto$ Likelihood $\times$ Prior. Forms the core of spam filtering, intrusion detection, and Kalman filters.

slides.speaker_notes: Derive Bayes rule as the quotient of joint probability over total probability. Show visual shift from prior to posterior.

slides.title: Statistical Independence
slides.subtitle: Orthogonality vs Disjointness

theory_fragments.content: Two events $A$ and $B$ are **independent** ($A \perp B$) if and only if knowledge of $B$ does not perturb $A$:
P(A \mid B) = P(A) \iff P(A \cap B) = P(A) P(B)
Crucial CSE Fallacy: Disjoint events ($A \cap B = \emptyset$) with non-zero measure are NEVER independent! Since $P(A \cap B) = 0 \neq P(A)P(B)$.
Pairwise independence does NOT imply mutual independence: $\bigcap_{i=1}^n P(A_i) = \prod P(A_i)$ must hold for all sub-families.

slides.speaker_notes: Warn students against confusing disjoint sets with independent sets. Use the interactive canvas to contrast both cases.

slides.title: Random Variables & Distributions
slides.subtitle: Mapping Sample Spaces to $\mathbb{R}$

theory_fragments.content: A **random variable** $X$ is a measurable function $X: \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$. It maps outcomes to numerical values.
p_X(x) = P(X = x) = P(\{\omega \in \Omega : X(\omega) = x\})
The **Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF)** $F_X(x) = P(X \le x)$ is monotonically non-decreasing, right-continuous:
\lim_{x \to -\infty} F_X(x) = 0, \quad \lim_{x \to +\infty} F_X(x) = 1, \quad P(a < X \le b) = F_X(b) - F_X(a)

slides.speaker_notes: Clarify that random variables are deterministic functions from Omega to R, not variables in the standard programming sense.

slides.title: Linearity of Expectation
slides.subtitle: The Algorithmist's Master Key

theory_fragments.content: The **expected value** of a discrete random variable $X$ is the probability-weighted Lebesgue-Stieltjes sum:
\mathbb{E}[X] = \sum_{x \in \text{Im}(X)} x \cdot P(X = x)
Theorem (Linearity): For ANY random variables $X_1, \dots, X_n$ (even arbitrarily correlated and dependent):
\mathbb{E}\left[ \sum_{i=1}^n c_i X_i \right] = \sum_{i=1}^n c_i \mathbb{E}[X_i]

slides.speaker_notes: Highlight that Linearity of Expectation holds regardless of dependence, enabling exact average-case analysis of algorithms like Randomized Quicksort.

slides.title: Tail Inequalities & Concentration
slides.subtitle: Bounding Worst-Case Runtime Latencies

theory_fragments.content: In production systems, mean performance $\mathbb{E}[X]$ is insufficient. We must bound the probability of catastrophic deviations.
\text{Markov: } X \ge 0, a > 0 \implies P(X \ge a) \le \frac{\mathbb{E}[X]}{a}
\text{Chebyshev: } \sigma^2 = \text{Var}(X) \implies P(|X - \mu| \ge k\sigma) \le \frac{1}{k^2}
Higher moments yield exponentially tighter tail envelopes: Chernoff bound $P(X \ge (1+\delta)\mu) \le e^{-\mu\delta^2/3}$.

slides.speaker_notes: Contrast first-moment bounds (Markov) with second-moment bounds (Chebyshev) and demonstrate their decay rates on tail latency.

slides.title: Application: Bloom Filter Analysis
slides.subtitle: Probabilistic Space-Efficient Membership

theory_fragments.content: A **Bloom Filter** represents set $S$ with $|S|=n$ using $m$ bits and $k$ independent uniform hash functions $h_i(x) \in [m]$.
P(\text{bit } j \text{ remains 0 after } n \text{ insertions}) = \left(1 - \frac{1}{m}\right)^{kn} \approx e^{-kn/m}
P(\text{False Positive}) = \left(1 - \left(1 - \frac{1}{m}\right)^{kn}\right)^k \approx (1 - e^{-kn/m})^k
Optimal hash count minimizing false positives: $k^* = \frac{m}{n} \ln 2 \implies P(\text{FP}) \approx (0.6185)^{m/n}$.

slides.speaker_notes: Complete the arc by connecting Kolmogorov axioms, independence, and limits to an optimal data structure used in databases and routers.

slides.title: Synthesis & Algorithmic Principles
slides.subtitle: The Foundations of Randomized Computing

theory_fragments.content: Probability theory provides exact deterministic metrics for unpredictable execution environments.
**Axiomatic Grounding:** $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, P)$ guarantees consistency across discrete and continuous program spaces.
**Conditional Inversion:** Bayes' Theorem and Total Probability partition complex state transitions into manageable conditional paths.
**Concentration & Tail Risk:** Linearity of Expectation calculates average runtime; Markov, Chebyshev, and Chernoff bound SLA violation risks.
Next Lecture: Continuous Random Variables, Probability Density Functions (PDFs), and Central Limit Theorem in High-Throughput Streaming.

slides.speaker_notes: Summarize the core takeaways. Connect the mathematical framework to production software engineering and announce the next lecture topic.

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="UTF-8">
<style>
  body { margin: 0; background: #0f172a; overflow: hidden; font-family: monospace; user-select: none; }
  canvas { display: block; width: 100vw; height: 100vh; }
</style>
</head>
<body>
<canvas id="stage" width="800" height="600"></canvas>
<script>
const canvas = document.getElementById('stage');
const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');

let currentStep = 1;
const maxSteps = 4;
const stepDescriptions = [
    "Initial network topology",
    "Simulating link failures with probability p",
    "Probability of at least one link failure",
    "Formalizing uncertainty: Probability Space"
];

// --- Canvas & Projection Settings ---
const CANVAS_WIDTH = 800;
const CANVAS_HEIGHT = 600;
const CENTER_X = CANVAS_WIDTH / 2;
const CENTER_Y = CANVAS_HEIGHT / 2;
const FOCAL_LENGTH = 300; // For perspective projection

// --- 3D Scene Variables ---
let nodes = [];
let links = [];
const NUM_NODES = 60; // Visualized nodes
const NODE_RADIUS = 6;
const P_VISUAL_FAILURE = 0.08; // Probability of link failure for visualization
const SYSTEM_RADIUS = 180; // Radius of the sphere arrangement

let yaw = 0.0;
let pitch = 0.0;
let drag = false;
let lastX, lastY;

// --- Node structure ---
class Node {
    constructor(id, x, y, z) {
        this.id = id;
        this.x = x;
        this.y = y;
        this.z = z;
        this.projected = { x: 0, y: 0, scale: 0, z: 0 };
    }

    project() {
        // Apply rotation
        let rx = this.x, ry = this.y, rz = this.z;

        // Rotate around Y-axis (yaw)
        let temp_x = rx * Math.cos(yaw) + rz * Math.sin(yaw);
        let temp_z = -rx * Math.sin(yaw) + rz * Math.cos(yaw);
        rx = temp_x;
        rz = temp_z;

        // Rotate around X-axis (pitch)
        let temp_y = ry * Math.cos(pitch) - rz * Math.sin(pitch);
        temp_z = ry * Math.sin(pitch) + rz * Math.cos(pitch);
        ry = temp_y;
        rz = temp_z;

        // Perspective projection
        // Cap minimum depth to prevent infinite scaling (nodes too close to focal point)
        const minZ = -FOCAL_LENGTH + 10; // Ensure z is always > minZ
        const effectiveZ = Math.max(minZ, rz);
        const scale = FOCAL_LENGTH / (FOCAL_LENGTH + effectiveZ);
        this.projected.x = CENTER_X + rx * scale;
        this.projected.y = CENTER_Y + ry * scale;
        this.projected.scale = scale;
        this.projected.z = effectiveZ; // Store for depth sorting
    }

    draw(ctx, isFailed = false) {
        ctx.beginPath();
        ctx.arc(this.projected.x, this.projected.y, NODE_RADIUS * this.projected.scale, 0, Math.PI * 2);
        ctx.fillStyle = isFailed ? '#f43f5e' : '#00E5FF';
        ctx.fill();
        ctx.strokeStyle = '#334155';
        ctx.lineWidth = 1 * this.projected.scale;
        ctx.stroke();
    }
}

// --- Link structure ---
class Link {
    constructor(node1, node2) {
        this.node1 = node1;
        this.node2 = node2;
        this.failed = false;
        this.projected_z = 0; // Average Z for depth sorting
    }

    // Update projected_z after nodes are projected
    updateProjectedZ() {
        this.projected_z = (this.node1.projected.z + this.node2.projected.z) / 2;
    }

    draw(ctx) {
        ctx.beginPath();
        ctx.moveTo(this.node1.projected.x, this.node1.projected.y);
        ctx.lineTo(this.node2.projected.x, this.node2.projected.y);
        ctx.strokeStyle = this.failed ? '#f43f5e' : '#10b981';
        ctx.lineWidth = 2 * Math.min(this.node1.projected.scale, this.node2.projected.scale);
        ctx.stroke();
    }
}

function initNodesAndLinks() {
    nodes = [];
    links = [];
    
    // Arrange nodes on a sphere (Fibonacci sphere / golden spiral distribution)
    for (let i = 0; i < NUM_NODES; i++) {
        const phi = Math.acos(1 - (2 * i) / (NUM_NODES - 1)); // latitude
        const theta = Math.PI * (1 + Math.sqrt(5)) * i; // longitude (golden angle)

        const x = SYSTEM_RADIUS * Math.cos(theta) * Math.sin(phi);
        const y = SYSTEM_RADIUS * Math.sin(theta) * Math.sin(phi);
        const z = SYSTEM_RADIUS * Math.cos(phi);
        nodes.push(new Node(i, x, y, z));
    }

    // Create a mesh-like structure by connecting to a few nearest neighbors
    // This approximates a distributed system without a full mesh.
    const connectionsPerNode = 4; 
    const tempLinks = new Set(); // Use a Set to avoid duplicate links

    for (let i = 0; i < NUM_NODES; i++) {
        const currentNode = nodes[i];
        const distances = [];
        for (let j = 0; j < NUM_NODES; j++) {
            if (i === j) continue;
            const otherNode = nodes[j];
            const dist = Math.sqrt(
                (currentNode.x - otherNode.x)**2 +
                (currentNode.y - otherNode.y)**2 +
                (currentNode.z - otherNode.z)**2
            );
            distances.push({ node: otherNode, dist: dist });
        }

        distances.sort((a, b) => a.dist - b.dist);

        for (let k = 0; k < Math.min(connectionsPerNode, distances.length); k++) {
            const targetNode = distances[k].node;
            const linkKey = `${Math.min(currentNode.id, targetNode.id)}-${Math.max(currentNode.id, targetNode.id)}`;
            if (!tempLinks.has(linkKey)) {
                links.push(new Link(currentNode, targetNode));
                tempLinks.add(linkKey);
            }
        }
    }
}

initNodesAndLinks(); // Initialize once

// --- State Variables for Telemetry ---
let failedLinkCount = 0;
let probabilityOfAtLeastOneFailure = 0;

function updateSimulationState() {
    failedLinkCount = 0;
    if (currentStep >= 2) {
        for (const link of links) {
            link.failed = Math.random() < P_VISUAL_FAILURE;
            if (link.failed) {
                failedLinkCount++;
            }
        }
        // Calculate P(at least one link failure) for the *visualized* system
        const totalLinks = links.length;
        if (totalLinks > 0) {
             probabilityOfAtLeastOneFailure = 1 - Math.pow((1 - P_VISUAL_FAILURE), totalLinks);
        } else {
             probabilityOfAtLeastOneFailure = 0;
        }
       
    } else {
        for (const link of links) {
            link.failed = false;
        }
    }
}

function advanceToStep(step) {
    currentStep = Math.max(1, Math.min(maxSteps, step));
    updateSimulationState(); // Re-evaluate link failures on step change
}

// --- Animation Loop ---
function animate() {
    // Clear canvas
    ctx.fillStyle = '#0f172a';
    ctx.fillRect(0, 0, CANVAS_WIDTH, CANVAS_HEIGHT);

    // Update and Project all nodes
    for (const node of nodes) {
        node.project();
    }

    // Update Z for links and prepare all renderable objects for depth sorting
    let renderableObjects = [];
    for (const node of nodes) {
        renderableObjects.push({ type: 'node', obj: node, z: node.projected.z });
    }
    for (const link of links) {
        link.updateProjectedZ();
        renderableObjects.push({ type: 'link', obj: link, z: link.projected_z });
    }

    // Depth sort (Painter's Algorithm) - draw farthest first
    renderableObjects.sort((a, b) => b.z - a.z); // Sort by Z, farthest (largest Z) first

    // Draw objects
    for (const item of renderableObjects) {
        if (item.type === 'link') {
            if (currentStep === 1) {
                 // On step 1, all links are considered active for visualization
                 // (even if updateSimulationState set some to failed, we override visually)
                const originalFailedState = item.obj.failed;
                item.obj.failed = false;
                item.obj.draw(ctx);
                item.obj.failed = originalFailedState; // Restore for next step
            } else {
                 item.obj.draw(ctx);
            }
        } else if (item.type === 'node') {
            let isNodeInFailedLink = false;
            if (currentStep >= 2) {
                for (const link of links) {
                    if (link.failed && (link.node1 === item.obj || link.node2 === item.obj)) {
                        isNodeInFailedLink = true;
                        break;
                    }
                }
            }
            item.obj.draw(ctx, isNodeInFailedLink && currentStep >= 2);
        }
    }

    // --- HUD ---
    ctx.fillStyle = '#00E5FF';
    ctx.font = '16px monospace';
    ctx.fillText('Uncertainty in Distributed Systems', 20, 30);

    ctx.fillStyle = '#fbbf24';
    ctx.font = '14px monospace';
    ctx.fillText(`Step ${currentStep}/${maxSteps}: ${stepDescriptions[currentStep - 1]}`, 20, 55);

    ctx.fillStyle = '#10b981';
    ctx.font = '14px monospace';
    let telemetryText = `Nodes: ${NUM_NODES}, Links: ${links.length}`;
    if (currentStep >= 2) {
        telemetryText += `, p_visual: ${P_VISUAL_FAILURE.toFixed(3)}`;
        telemetryText += `, Failed Links: ${failedLinkCount}`;
    }
    if (currentStep >= 3) {
        telemetryText += `, P(at least 1 fail): ${(probabilityOfAtLeastOneFailure * 100).toFixed(3)}%`;
    }
    ctx.fillText(telemetryText, 20, 80);

    ctx.fillStyle = '#64748b';
    ctx.font = '12px monospace';
    ctx.fillText('Click Left: Prev Step | Click Right: Next Step | Drag: Orbit View', 20, 580);

    requestAnimationFrame(animate);
}

// --- Event Listeners ---
let startX, startY, startTime;
window.addEventListener('pointerdown', e => {
    startX = e.clientX;
    startY = e.clientY;
    startTime = Date.now();
    drag = true;
    lastX = e.clientX;
    lastY = e.clientY;
});

window.addEventListener('pointermove', e => {
    if (drag) {
        const dx = e.clientX - lastX;
        const dy = e.clientY - lastY;
        yaw += dx * 0.005;
        pitch -= dy * 0.005; // Invert for more intuitive vertical drag
        
        // Clamp pitch to prevent flipping
        pitch = Math.max(-Math.PI / 2, Math.min(Math.PI / 2, pitch));
        
        lastX = e.clientX;
        lastY = e.clientY;
    }
});

window.addEventListener('pointerup', e => {
    drag = false;
    if (Math.abs(e.clientX - startX) < 15 && Math.abs(e.clientY - startY) < 15 && Date.now() - startTime < 350) {
        if (e.clientX < window.innerWidth / 3) {
            advanceToStep(currentStep - 1);
        } else {
            advanceToStep(currentStep + 1);
        }
    }
});

// Initial call to start the animation
initNodesAndLinks();
advanceToStep(1); // Set initial step and state
animate();

</script>
</body>
</html>

<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="UTF-8">
<style>body { margin: 0; background: #0f172a; overflow: hidden; font-family: monospace; user-select: none; } canvas { display: block; width: 100vw; height: 100vh; }</style>

<body>
<canvas id="stage" width="800" height="600"></canvas>
<script>
const canvas = document.getElementById('stage');
const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
let currentStep = 1; const maxSteps = 4;
let startX, startY, startTime;
window.addEventListener('pointerdown', e => { startX = e.clientX; startY = e.clientY; startTime = Date.now(); });
window.addEventListener('pointerup', e => {
  if (Math.abs(e.clientX - startX) < 15 && Math.abs(e.clientY - startY) < 15 && Date.now() - startTime < 350) {
    if (e.clientX < window.innerWidth / 3) { currentStep = Math.max(1, currentStep - 1); }
    else { currentStep = Math.min(maxSteps, currentStep + 1); }
    advanceToStep(currentStep);
  }
});
function advanceToStep(s) { currentStep = s; }

function render() {
  ctx.fillStyle = '#0f172a'; ctx.fillRect(0, 0, 800, 600);

  // Draw Universal Set Omega
  ctx.strokeStyle = '#64748b'; ctx.lineWidth = 2;
  ctx.strokeRect(150, 140, 500, 360);
  ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(100, 116, 139, 0.1)'; ctx.fillRect(150, 140, 500, 360);
  ctx.font = '16px monospace'; ctx.fillStyle = '#64748b'; ctx.fillText('Universal Sample Space Ω', 165, 165);

  // Base circle positions
  const c1x = 340, c1y = 320, r1 = 110;
  const c2x = 460, c2y = 320, r2 = 110;

  if (currentStep === 1) {
    ctx.strokeStyle = '#00E5FF'; ctx.lineWidth = 2; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(c1x, c1y, r1, 0, Math.PI*2); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.strokeStyle = '#10b981'; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(c2x, c2y, r2, 0, Math.PI*2); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.fillStyle = '#00E5FF'; ctx.fillText('Event A', 270, 320);
    ctx.fillStyle = '#10b981'; ctx.fillText('Event B', 490, 320);
  } else if (currentStep === 2) {
    // Complement A^c
    ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(244, 63, 94, 0.2)'; ctx.fillRect(150, 140, 500, 360);
    ctx.save();
    ctx.globalCompositeOperation = 'destination-out';
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(c1x, c1y, r1, 0, Math.PI*2); ctx.fill();
    ctx.restore();
    ctx.strokeStyle = '#00E5FF'; ctx.lineWidth = 3; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(c1x, c1y, r1, 0, Math.PI*2); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.fillStyle = '#f43f5e'; ctx.fillText('Complement A^c = Ω \\ A', 165, 480);
  } else if (currentStep === 3) {
    // Intersection A cap B
    ctx.save();
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(c1x, c1y, r1, 0, Math.PI*2); ctx.clip();
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(c2x, c2y, r2, 0, Math.PI*2);
    ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(251, 191, 36, 0.6)'; ctx.fill();
    ctx.restore();
    ctx.strokeStyle = '#00E5FF'; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(c1x, c1y, r1, 0, Math.PI*2); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.strokeStyle = '#10b981'; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(c2x, c2y, r2, 0, Math.PI*2); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.fillStyle = '#fbbf24'; ctx.fillText('Intersection A ∩ B', 340, 325);
  } else if (currentStep === 4) {
    // Union A cup B
    ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(0, 229, 255, 0.3)';
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(c1x, c1y, r1, 0, Math.PI*2); ctx.fill();
    ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(16, 185, 129, 0.3)';
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(c2x, c2y, r2, 0, Math.PI*2); ctx.fill();
    ctx.strokeStyle = '#fbbf24'; ctx.lineWidth = 2.5;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(c1x, c1y, r1, 0, Math.PI*2); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(c2x, c2y, r2, 0, Math.PI*2); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.fillStyle = '#ffffff'; ctx.fillText('Union A ∪ B ∈ F', 360, 325);
  }

  // HUD Telemetry Header
  ctx.font = '16px monospace'; ctx.fillStyle = '#00E5FF';
  ctx.fillText('Sigma-Algebra & Set Measure Topology', 20, 30);
  ctx.font = '14px monospace'; ctx.fillStyle = '#fbbf24';
  const desc = ['Primitive Event Subsets in Ω', 'Closure Under Complement A^c', 'Closure Under Intersection A ∩ B', 'Closure Under Countable Union A ∪ B'][currentStep-1];
  ctx.fillText('Step ' + currentStep + '/' + maxSteps + ': ' + desc, 20, 55);
